subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Which owner boundary should take the first bounded repair: runner-capacity and timeout diagnostics, the live GitHub HTTP fixture, or local-auth profile retry/query behavior?
rationale: These are independent failure modes with different validation environments; choosing the first lane determines whether a repair is CI-provider configuration, test-harness resilience, or application query behavior.

options.title: Start with runner diagnostics
options.body: Add short-lived or permanent capacity and timeout diagnostics, then use the measured result to choose the smallest follow-up fix.

options.title: Harden the HTTP fixture first
options.body: Add bounded retry only for identified retryable GitHub lookup failures while preserving clear failure for confirmed missing repositories.

options.title: Reduce local-auth amplification first
options.body: Replace broad navigation retries with readiness-aware polling and avoid inactive profile subscriptions before reassessing runner capacity.

recommendation.title: Start with runner diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add short-lived or permanent capacity and timeout diagnostics, then use the measured result to choose the smallest follow-up fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged CI reliability work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for a decision spanning workflow diagnostics and retry policy.
